audit_findings.title: Core lease-financing income may have been incorrectly purged
audit_findings.magnitude: $14.093m of 2025 interest revenue, equal to 29.9% of the $47.1m OE anchor; related notes receivable and sales-type leases totaled $156.540m at 2025 year-end
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing core lease-financing interest reduces OE, while failure to add the related financial assets separately also understates the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest revenue represents interest earned on notes receivable related to failed sale-leasebacks in which the Company was the buyer-lessor and on sales-type leases.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that reported interest revenue came from failed sale-leasebacks and sales-type leases integral to leasing operations. The record does not demonstrate exactly what the OE reconciliation removed. If the full $14.093m was purged without separately valuing the $156.540m of related assets, the omission is large enough to materially raise every scenario when corrected.
audit_findings.action: Produce the 2025 OE reconciliation by interest-income source; restore interest from operating notes and sales-type leases, or separately value the corresponding assets, then rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method stakes may be counted both in OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.365m of 2025 equity-method income and $104.6m bridge addition; the income equals 28.4% of the $47.1m OE anchor and the bridge addition equals 13.5% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If equity-method income remains in OE, the DCF capitalizes that income while the bridge independently adds the value of the same investments.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s investments are joint ventures which are accounted for using the equity method of accounting.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that $13.365m of joint-venture income entered 2025 reported earnings and that the investments were carried at $104.250m. Whether OE removed that income is unresolved. Retaining it while adding $104.6m of stakes would be material double counting.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to reported earnings and identify all equity-method income and distributions; remove the income before applying the DCF if the stakes remain in the bridge, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor could retain a disposal gain nearly as large as OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $43.0m pre-tax disposal gain, equal to 91.3% of the $47.1m OE anchor; after-tax OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained disposal gain inflates anchor OE and is then grown and capitalized through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The transaction closed on June 30, 2025, resulting in a gain on sale of business of approximately $43.0 million for the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The $43.0m BAML gain is demonstrated and nonrecurring, but its treatment in the OE reconciliation is not supplied. Because it is nearly the entire anchor, even substantial partial retention could change the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2025 OE reconciliation and tax workpaper for the BAML sale; verify removal of the complete after-tax gain and associated working-capital, deferred-gain, and transaction effects, then rerun the valuation if any amount remains.

audit_findings.title: Committed overhaul costs may escape the reinvestment charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $106.6m-$132.1m estimated through 2030, potentially up to $172.7m through 2035
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncaptured overhaul cash costs overstate OE by understating maintenance reinvestment and may mismatch maintenance-reserve revenue with the later cash expenditure.
audit_findings.evidence: As part of the purchase, we have committed to certain future overhaul and maintenance services which are anticipated to range between $106.6 million and $131.9 million by 2030.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual service obligation and its filed cost range are demonstrated; omission from OE is not. The lower estimate is more than twice the $47.1m annual anchor, so its timing and existing coverage must be established before the valuation can rely on the reinvestment charge.
audit_findings.action: Map the committed engines, expected service dates, maintenance-reserve receipts, capitalized overhaul additions, reimbursements, and OE maintenance-capex deductions; rerun the DCF with any uncovered annual cash costs.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable preferred stock may remain an unbridged senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $65.0m redemption principal plus $1.1m accrued dividends, or approximately $66.1m; $2.52 per diluted share and 8.5% of $777.0m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Preferred dividends and accretion affect common OE, while redemption principal and unpaid dividends are a senior claim that may require a separate equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: The redemption price is $20.00 per share plus dividends accrued but not paid.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge visibly contains no preferred-stock deduction, but the record does not establish whether forecast OE explicitly funds redemption. A separate $66.1m deduction would reduce base value from $29.65 to approximately $27.13 per share, a material change even though it would not reverse the conclusion relative to the $56.22 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether anchor OE is after preferred dividends and accretion and whether forecast cash flows explicitly fund redemption; if not, deduct redemption value plus accrued unpaid dividends from the common-equity bridge and recompute value per share and buy-below.

audit_findings.title: Convertible shares and the earnings numerator may describe different claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 2.232120m conversion shares, equal to 8.5% of the 26.205159m denominator; $5.0m annual pre-tax coupon and approximately $3.7m after tax using the filed 26.1% interim effective tax rate
audit_findings.mechanism: Assumed-conversion shares dilute value per share, while retaining the convertible note's interest reduces OE; applying both describes inconsistent capital structures.
audit_findings.evidence: Common stock equivalents are not included in diluted earnings per share when their inclusion is anti-dilutive.
audit_findings.explanation: The denominator includes the conversion shares and the stated method generally retains interest expense, but the record does not show how the post-anchor convertible coupon was incorporated. The possible mismatch is unresolved rather than a demonstrated error. Its share and coupon scale is sufficient to materially affect per-share value.
audit_findings.action: Prepare an as-converted versus unconverted reconciliation for every forecast year; either retain the 2.232120m shares and exclude the note's after-tax interest, or retain the interest and remove those shares until conversion is assumed, then rerun all scenarios.
